issues.legal_issue: A later suit challenging a threat to disconnect and the resulting disconnection is not barred by res judicata when the earlier suit concerned a different matter and sought different relief.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought a permanent injunction against enforcement of a demand for the previous occupant’s electricity arrears and was dismissed, with the dismissal affirmed.
The later suit challenged a threat to disconnect the electricity supply and the resulting disconnection, and sought a declaration and consequential relief.
The matters directly and substantially in issue, and the reliefs sought, differed between the two suits.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was not barred by res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata does not bar a subsequent suit when the matter directly and substantially in issue in it is different from the matter in the earlier suit; the court also relied on the difference in relief sought in the two suits.

rule.if: successive_civil_suits and earlier_suit_final and issues_materially_differ and reliefs_differ

predicates.successive_civil_suits: A party brought a later civil suit after an earlier civil suit concerning the same dispute.
predicates.earlier_suit_final: The earlier suit ended in a final decision.
predicates.issues_materially_differ: The matters directly and substantially in issue in the two suits were different.
predicates.reliefs_differ: The relief sought in the later suit differed from the relief sought in the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a final earlier suit is followed by a later suit whose central issues and requested relief differ, the later suit is not barred by res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent purchaser cannot be required to pay a previous occupant’s electricity arrears unless an applicable statutory rule or binding term of supply authorizes recovery from the purchaser.
material_facts: A financial corporation auctioned the premises of a borrower to recover its dues, and the purchaser paid the full auction price.
Electricity supply had been disconnected before the auction; the purchaser took possession and obtained a new electricity connection in its own name.
The electricity supplier later demanded arrears incurred by the previous owner and disconnected supply when the purchaser did not pay.
The supplier did not plead or identify any statutory rule or binding term of supply authorizing it to demand the previous owner’s arrears from the purchaser.

The supplier had not demanded those arrears when the purchaser obtained the new connection; the enabling term referred to in the cited later decision had been introduced after the connection was obtained.
issues.conclusion: The previous owner’s electricity arrears could not be enforced against the purchaser on these facts, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Electricity arrears do not, as a matter of general law, constitute a charge on the premises, and a purchaser with no contractual relationship to the previous occupant is not ordinarily liable for that occupant’s dues. Under Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board, a fresh connection cannot be made conditional on payment of prior arrears absent a charge or an authorizing statutory rule. Paramount Polymers distinguished Isha Marbles where a binding term of supply expressly authorized recovery from a transferee; Hyderabad Vanaspati Ltd. v. A.P. SEB held that terms notified under Section 49 of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 are statutory in character. Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Excel Buildcon Pvt. Ltd. followed Paramount Polymers. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd. reiterated that prior dues are not a charge, but may be demanded where applicable rules or binding terms authorize it, provided they are not arbitrary or unreasonable. The court found no such authorization applicable to this case; it did not need to decide whether an authorized term would be invalid on other grounds.

rule.if: prior_electricity_dues_recovery_claim and subsequent_purchaser_seeks_supply and purchaser_not_previous_consumer and not binding_supply_rule_authorizes_prior_dues

predicates.prior_electricity_dues_recovery_claim: An electricity supplier sought to recover charges incurred by a previous occupant from a later purchaser of the premises.
predicates.subsequent_purchaser_seeks_supply: A purchaser of premises sought a new or restored electricity supply for those premises.
predicates.purchaser_not_previous_consumer: The purchaser was not the consumer who incurred the electricity charges and had no contractual relationship with that consumer’s supplier.
predicates.binding_supply_rule_authorizes_prior_due: An applicable binding rule or term of supply authorized the supplier to require payment of the previous occupant’s arrears from the purchaser.
predicates.previous_occupant_dues_not_recoverable_f: The previous occupant’s electricity arrears cannot be recovered from the subsequent purchaser.

issues.definition: If a supplier seeks a previous occupant’s electricity arrears from a purchaser seeking supply, and the purchaser was not the previous consumer, the arrears are not recoverable from the purchaser when no applicable binding rule authorizes that recovery.
